purpose: Independent original-window ledger and actual-action comparison of old 6cc Native evidence and new 6414 Native evidence. This is a diagnostic proof, not production acceptance.
rules: Use the exact source checkpoint windows including email authentication, Native PKCE/session handoff, workspace navigation, concurrent background work and original FIRST pair 1.
Do not extend a window, substitute a later pair, move SQL across a boundary, deduct unknown/background counts, rerun a job, or reinterpret functional success as budget success.
Statement comparison uses command + normalizedStructureId + parameterCount, never local statement indexes. Known context grouping uses original rpcAction/route and invocation identifiers.
Cross-run temporal-occurrence matching is descriptive only. No claim of equal request arguments, returned data, database contents or cache state is made from redacted diagnostic metadata.
All source bytes were fetched from immutable Git blobs. No original Actions job log or ZIP was downloaded, no source/ref was changed, and no VM/cloud resource was allocated by this analysis.

method.ledger: For every original checkpoint, segment and total, independently sum 17 operation buckets to queryCalls and 78 source buckets to unattributed. Verify five cumulative counter differences and every bucket difference between adjacent checkpoints, and segment sums to each total.
method.ordinals: Verify all captured window rows are contiguous from fromQueryCalls+1 through toQueryCalls, match original checkpoint endpoints and expected/captured totals, map original scope indexes to operation/source counts, and recompute unknown-context/statement counts. Verify segment ordinal endpoints and capture loss/overflow flags.
method.requestBoundaries: Read original physical and logical action matrices and cross-check the four new hosted FIRST crossing receipts. Completion after the window is diagnostic metadata only; later SQL is never added.
method.statementScope: Count each statement structure within its original context and scope. Unknown statements remain explicit; statement hashes do not reveal SQL text or bound parameter values.

measurement.clock: Node performance.now, immediately before Electron launch to visible seeded message and enabled composer accepting a draft
measurement.process: same compiled shell/backend, bundled vs preserved hosted loading path; fresh Electron process for every sample, existing authenticated profile, same account/workspace
measurement.cache: normal profile/OS caches; no OS cache purge, artificial network delay or renderer response substitution
measurement.daemon: after every sample, cancel installers, close Electron and prove that exact profile daemon exited before launching the next process; drain time is outside readiness timing
measurement.preparation: one owned installed-app profile; both loading modes must reach a real registered online local device before the unchanged cold samples

identicalDeclarationsAndCleanup.queryBackground: all concurrent primary API background traffic is included; no guessed subtraction or per-request attribution
queryExclusions: test-account lease/session tracking and fixture SQL in the separate harness process
PostgreSQL connection handshake and TCP/TLS overhead
identicalDeclarationsAndCleanup.queryBoundary: query calls started and protocol bytes transferred by each checkpoint; in-flight response bytes can cross a checkpoint

observedFindings: Old Native full login is 19 + 15 + 391 = 425; new is 19 + 15 + 399 = 433. PKCE is unchanged at 15, and its exact operation/source buckets are unchanged.

Native full-login +8 is entirely in the workspace segment: issues.syncIssueList +4, coordinator.syncCoordinatorChat +2, coordinator.pollBotChatSummaries +1, task-runs.pollTaskRuns +1. Full-login unknown context remains 91; all unattributed source counts are unchanged.

All 40 Native full-login logical starts/completions and per-action frequencies are unchanged. Physical starts/completions rise 14 to 16: desktop.readBatch decreases 8 to 7 while bots.pollBots, summaries and syncCoordinatorChat each gain one standalone HTTP call.

The fourth summaries call changes 7 to 8 SQL and the fourth syncCoordinatorChat call 19 to 21 SQL. They share an old HTTP batch but are separate new HTTP invocations. Their extra stable shapes are 6eda258b3007(p4) twice and 82919a1d33a6(p1) once. Causal memo semantics require separate source analysis.

The fourth issues call changes 4 to 8: SELECT 9f0fe8477a06(p2) +1 and unknown statement +3. The first task-runs call changes 5 to 6, solely SELECT 9f0fe8477a06(p2) +1. Other temporal occurrences of these four actions have identical statement-count bags.

Web full login decreases 435 to 431 solely through coordinator.syncCoordinatorChat 104 to 100, with identical logical/physical frequencies. All four fewer statements have unknown structure, so their exact SQL cannot be named.

Native original FIRST decreases 213 to 209, with unchanged 19 logical calls and fewer physical calls (8 to 6). Its -4 is bots.pollBots -1 and teams.listTeams -1, both SELECT 6eda258b3007(p4), plus issues -2 consisting of SELECT 9f0fe8477a06(p2) -1 and unknown statement -1.

Hosted original FIRST decreases 220 to 147. It has four fewer logical starts (summaries, task-runs, project-teams and teams each 2 to 1) and four original-window crossing completions: syncCoordinatorChat twice, model menu once and issues once.

The new hosted FIRST crossing completions occur 23ms, 33ms, 98ms and 144ms after the exact endpoint. Their measured SQL and all original endpoints remain unchanged at total 147. These observations do not license adding later SQL.

Across all four measured windows both runs contain the same 75 known (command, structureId, parameterCount) signatures; no new signature is observed. Frequency and context location change, which does not prove equality of full SQL text or data.

Known after:* source buckets, /v1/* source buckets and noScope all have zero window deltas in both runs; otherScoped is 10 in every window and remains included. This does not prove that unclassified work is absent.

Cleanup stages and native-resource cleanup counts are identical and successful. The measurement/cache rules are identical. Both modes in a given run use the same daemon, but cross-run daemon changes from 0.0.562 / 111a8dfb8b227ac0441324339ff42e4328ea609a to 0.0.564 / 8db16095f46be955df22f42914e0f89b6e5f3d11, so App changes alone are not an isolated causal treatment.
remainingUnknowns: New Native full-login 91 queries have unknown invocation context, and 132 have unknown statement structure; these sets overlap and must not be summed. Context-unknown counts do not change cross-run, but that is not proof of identical hidden work.

Exactly three of the +8 Native full-login queries are unknown statement shapes within a known issues.syncIssueList invocation. Their exact SQL and business purpose cannot be established from the source artifact.
The three increased known signatures are not translated into SQL text here; source review must establish their definitions, memoization and state/cache paths.
Unchanged fixture labels, profile declarations or cleanup counts do not establish equivalent mutable database/profile/cache state between runs.
One observed old/new pair does not identify a stochastic cause or justify rerunning for a favorable outcome. Original budget failures remain failures.

membershipShapeBatchOwnership.interpretation: The old five-member batch contains issues, task-runs, threads, summaries and coordinator chat. The new five-member batch contains issues, task-runs, threads, teams and project-teams, while summaries and chat are standalone. The shape occurs once under task-runs in each batch, and once in each new standalone request. This is an exact metadata observation; SQL mapping and memo semantics are handled in the separate source review.
